AlternateTargets: the eye that selects the teaching
Senses.Explanation: A faculty or criterion for seeing and selecting the teaching. One direct definition says, 'nowhere not pervasive and nowhere not clear; therefore it is called the eye of the teaching.' In a recorded case, an unnamed participant asks what the eye of the teaching is and receives, 'the eye of the teaching has no flaw.' The productive phrase 'an eye that selects the teaching' appears in challenges to distinguish black from white and in the requirement that a lineage teacher possess such an eye. Transmission narratives also contain the pure eye of the teaching within an entrustment formula. These definitions, questions, compounds, and transmission uses establish a teaching faculty or criterion, not the person Fayan Wenyi.
Senses.Note: The headword has 5,130 occurrences in 380 allowlisted texts. The larger correct-eye-of-the-teaching compounds account for many hits and have their own entries or cross-references. The title-name Fayan is handled separately below.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Master Qianyan (千巖和尚語錄). Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Qianyan Yuanzhang as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰如何是法眼曰法眼無瑕
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Pearls Linking Verses on Old Cases in the Chan Lineage (禪宗頌古聯珠通集), in the narrative leading Jiashan Shanhui to Chuanzi Decheng. An unnamed participant asks Jiashan what the eye of the teaching is, and Jiashan Shanhui is the exact respondent who says that this eye has no flaw. The headword graphs here name the eye of the teaching, not the later title-name Fayan Wenyi.

Senses.Explanation: The title-name Fayan identifies Fayan Wenyi. Catalogue headings count the lineage heirs of Great Fayan Wenyi of Qingliang in Jinling, commentaries introduce his turns with 'Fayan Yi said,' and a biography heading names Chan Master Fayan Wenyi of Qingliang before narrating his travels with Shaoxiu and Fajin. These personal predicates and roster relations identify a lineage person, not the eye or faculty described in the common noun sense.
Senses.Note: Fayan lineage occurs 134 times, the full name Fayan Wenyi 24 times, and the quotation formula Fayan said 179 times. This is a proper-name collision rather than a person-specific innovation in the common noun.
